requirements.summary: The same two files and directory structure are present after repair and restart, with SHA-256 hashes matching the preparation baseline and pre-change observation.

requirements.requirement: Ensure the existing inventory data is owned by inventorysvc.
requirements.summary: The required identity exists, and final direct metadata shows inventorysvc owns the root directory, data directory, and both existing files.

requirements.requirement: Make the inventory data readable by inventory-readers.
requirements.summary: All entries have inventory-readers group ownership with directory mode 750 and file mode 640. A non-owner process using that group successfully traversed the directories and read both files before and after restart.
Final modes grant no permissions to the other class, and an unrelated UID/GID was directly shown unable to read or traverse the inventory tree before and after restart.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final-state and behavioral evidence. The repaired permissions, identities, access controls, and unchanged contents persisted across a fully evidenced node restart.
limitations: Requirement preserve-existing-contents cited unknown evidence IDs: prepared-inventory-data

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the missing identities and repairing ownership and modes directly served the contract. The reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. Temporary health-probe files were removed within their successful commands, and lifecycle snapshots show no new temporary-file or package-health residue. The restart protocol is complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered services, identities, data, permissions, and access behavior; fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the transition.
